title: A welcome series for a high-ticket store
overview: Oakline sells solid wood sofas, tables and shelving. Most customers visit three or four times before buying, so the email system focuses on trust and education first, and the discount second.
problem: Long buying cycle. Visitors browse for weeks but get one discount email and nothing else.
why: Trust content comes before the discount, which suits orders above $500.
kpi_note: Targets are based on common industry benchmarks, not measured results.

flows.name: Welcome series
flows.description: Three emails over six days that introduce the brand, show best sellers and answer the most common buying questions.

emails.title: Email 1 · Your code is inside
emails.note: Delivers the 10% code and sets expectations for the next emails.

emails.title: Email 2 · How we build
emails.note: Shows the workshop and materials to build trust before asking for a sale.

emails.title: Email 3 · Best sellers
emails.note: Uses a conditional split so buyers do not get a sales push.

flows.name: Browse abandonment
flows.trigger: Viewed product, did not add to cart
flows.description: One reminder email showing the exact product the visitor looked at, with care details and reviews.

emails.title: Still thinking about it?
emails.note: Dynamic product block pulls the viewed item automatically.

campaigns.title: Autumn living room edit
campaigns.note: Seasonal campaign sent to engaged subscribers only (opened or clicked in the last 90 days).

title: A replenishment flow for repeat products
overview: Bloom Care sells a 30-day face serum. Revenue depends on reorders, so the email system follows the customer from first use to the moment the bottle runs out.
problem: Customers buy once and forget to reorder, even though the product lasts 30 days.
why: The reminder is timed to the product's real usage, so it feels helpful, not pushy.
kpi_note: Targets are based on common industry benchmarks, not measured results.

flows.name: Post-purchase
flows.description: Helps new customers use the product correctly, which leads to better results and more reorders.

emails.title: How to get the best results
How is your skin feeling?
emails.note: Review request with a one-click star rating.

flows.name: Replenishment
flows.description: Reminds customers to reorder just before the bottle runs out.

emails.title: Running low on your serum?
emails.note: One clear button that goes straight to checkout.

campaigns.title: Winter skin routine
campaigns.note: Educational campaign with a product bundle at the end.

title: Popup redesign and abandoned cart
overview: Ghor Spice Co. sells curated spice boxes. The store had steady traffic but a weak popup and no cart recovery, so the first fix was list growth and the second was recovering lost carts.
problem: The old popup appeared instantly, had no brand colours and offered "join our newsletter".
built: New branded popup with clear offer
why: A concrete reward and better timing give people a reason to sign up.
kpi_note: Targets are based on common industry benchmarks, not measured results.

flows.name: Abandoned cart
flows.description: Two reminders: a friendly nudge first, then a small incentive.

emails.title: You left something in the pot
emails.note: Shows the cart items and a single return-to-cart button.

emails.title: Free shipping if you finish today
emails.note: Adds an incentive only to people who did not return after email 1.

campaigns.title: Eid spice box launch
campaigns.note: Launch campaign with early access for VIP customers.
